title: The Water Cycle (KS2)
subject: Science
strapline: How water moves between the sea, sky and land — for ever.
facts: The water cycle is the never-ending journey of water around the Earth.
Evaporation: the sun heats water in seas, rivers and lakes and turns it into water vapour (a gas) that rises.
Condensation: high up it is cold, so the vapour cools and turns back into tiny droplets, forming clouds.
Precipitation: when the droplets get heavy they fall as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
Collection: the water flows into rivers and back to the sea, or soaks into the ground, and the cycle begins again.
The same water has been cycling for millions of years — no new water is made.
The sun is the energy that drives the whole cycle.

quick_quiz.q: What is it called when water vapour cools and forms clouds?
Name the stage where water falls as rain or snow.
What provides the energy for the water cycle?

teacher_tips: A sealed bag of water on a sunny window shows the cycle in miniature.
Use the four key words in order every time so the sequence sticks.
Link evaporation and condensation back to states of matter.
